chart.empty: No signal data for this period

signal.title: Signal Monitor
signal.summaryGood: Wireless devices: {{count}}, all with a good signal
signal.footer: Signal as the access point hears each device; refreshed every 2 seconds while this page is open.

detail.phoneNote: This is your phone. The signal shown is what the access point hears from it, which can differ from the phone's own reading.
detail.every2s: Updated every 2 seconds, kept only while this page is open
detail.needsPlugin: Install the RouteLink plugin to see signal history, roaming and retries.
detail.roamingNote: Connects and disconnects recorded by every router of the group.

tip.move-closer: The signal is weak. Move the device closer to the access point, or put the access point somewhere more open.
tip.add-ap: If the signal here is often poor, consider adding an access point nearby.
tip.rate-low: The link rate is under half of what this band usually gets: distance, interference or an older device may be the cause.
tip.none: The signal is fine; nothing to do.
tip.unknown: No signal data for this device yet.

roam.none: No connects or disconnects in this period

intruders.title: Who's on My Wi-Fi
intruders.empty: No devices online in this scope

setup.title: Mark your devices first
setup.message: At first every device counts as unknown. Tick the devices you recognise and trust them; from then on only new devices show as unknown.

pick.hint: {{count}} ticked. Ticked devices become trusted, unticked ones are no longer trusted.

intruders.kickTemporary: Kicking is temporary: anyone who knows the password can join again
intruders.localTrust: The trust list is kept on this phone and moves to the router once the plugin is installed.

note.kick: Kicking a device off is temporary: if it knows the password it will join again. Change the Wi-Fi password to keep it out.
note.private: Phones using a private (random) address show no vendor; that alone does not make them intruders.

channels.title: Channel Optimisation
channels.intro: Every radio of every access point in the group scans the air: see which channels nearby networks use and where yours would be better off.
channels.scanWarning: While scanning, an access point briefly leaves its channel: connected devices may stall for a second or two.
channels.unreachable: {{name}} is not connected and was not scanned
channels.none: No radio in the group can scan
channels.summaryKeep: All radios are on good channels
channels.dfsHint: DFS channels (52–144, and 36–48 at 160 MHz, whose block reaches 64) need a radar check first: after a switch the radio takes 1–10 minutes to come back, and it moves away by itself when it detects radar.

reason.keep-best: The current channel already has the least interference.
reason.keep-small-gain: No other channel is much better (interference would not even halve): better to stay.
reason.crowded-24: 2.4 GHz is crowded here: a 20 MHz channel is more robust.

channels.scanFailed: This radio did not finish its scan; the picture may be incomplete.
channels.noChannel: The radio's current channel is unknown, so there is no advice.

confirm.drop: Wi-Fi on this radio drops for a few seconds; devices reconnect by themselves
confirm.rollback: Applied safely: confirmed once the phone is back, otherwise the router restores the old setting
confirm.direct: The phone is on this radio and cannot confirm during the radar check: this change is not rolled back
confirm.dfs: On a DFS channel the radio may take 1–10 minutes to come back, and it moves to another channel if it detects radar

security.title: Security Check
security.unreachable: {{name}} is not connected: its Wi-Fi settings cannot be read
security.localOnly: Password strength is judged on this phone; the password is never sent anywhere.

levelHint.low: Outdated encryption that is easy to break.
levelHint.danger: No encryption or WEP: anyone can join or listen in.

finding.wps: WPS is on: its PIN can be brute-forced to get in.
finding.mfp-off: Management frame protection is off: forged disconnect frames can kick devices off.
finding.guest-not-isolated: The guest network does not isolate clients: guest devices can reach each other.
finding.hidden: Hiding the SSID adds no security; phones broadcast the name everywhere instead.

security.noSae: This router does not support WPA3 (SAE), so WPA2 stays. Installing the full wpad (e.g. wpad-mbedtls) makes the upgrade possible.
security.saeUnknown: Whether this router supports WPA3 (SAE) is unknown, so no upgrade is offered; change it in the Wi-Fi settings once you know it does.
security.share: Share the new password as a QR code
security.wpa3Hint: New devices use WPA3, older ones still join with WPA2
security.consequencePhoneBrief: Your phone is on this Wi-Fi: it drops for a few seconds and reconnects by itself
